PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Maternal Age: 27 years
Gestational Age: 13 weeks by ultrasound dating
Sample Type: Chorionic villi (uncultured)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing requested at 13 weeks gestation. Haemoglobinopathy testing indicated.

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured chorionic villi using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Multiple informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S858, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S11, D21S1270, D21S1411

DNA was extracted using standard protocols. PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for all informative markers.

RESULTS
Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed

Result: rsa(13,18,21)x2

No evidence of trisomy 13, trisomy 18, or trisomy 21 detected.

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis shows a normal chromosome complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 in this fetal sample. No abnormalities were detected for the chromosomes tested.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. It will not detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Segmental chromosomal imbalances
- Aneuploidies of other chromosomes
- Single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on these results, no further chromosome analysis is planned. The referring physician should correlate these findings with ultrasound results and other clinical information.

For haemoglobinopathy testing as indicated, please refer to separate report.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
